Marki Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Marki, Poland

Demolished. Jews are first confirmed in the Marki area (including villages later incorporated into the town, Pustelnik and Struga) from the early 19th century; a synagogue was built in 1826, and Jewish entrepreneurs (including Henryk Doktorowicz, St. Halber, and G. Goldberg) owned large local brickyards. By 1921, 156 Jews lived in Marki (6%), 368 in Pustelnik (14.5%), and 21 in Struga (3.2%); Rabbi Mosze Mendelshon led Pustelnik's community by the late 1930s. A 1940 ghetto occupied Doktorowicz's Osinka brickyard, holding Jews from Marki, Pustelnik, and Struga alongside displaced residents of Długosiodło, Mława, Serock, and Nasielsk; a March 1942 deportation to the Warsaw Ghetto preceded most residents' murder at Treblinka. This cemetery's exact location remains unknown, though sources place it in Pustelnik near modern Pomnikowa or Sienkiewicza Streets; likely established at the end of the 1930s, it probably held very few burials, and no mortuary ever stood there.
